newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali relatives in confusion over India disaster.
newsitem.headline: Nepali relatives in confusion over India disaster.

text.p: Relatives of the Nepali victims of the world's worst mid-air collision over India were in confusion on Wednesday as they were bombarded with conflicting information, officials said.
A Saudi newspaper said nine Nepalis were among the 350 victims of one of the five worst air disasters, but the only information available in Kathmandu made people fear a much worse toll.

"Relatives are inquiring about the victims but we have not received any confirmation from the concerned airlines," said Megh Lama, an official of the Gulf Manpower Services, a firm that sends Nepali labourers to Saudi Arabia.
Lama told Reuters his company had booked a group of 39 Nepali workers on the Saudi Arabia Airlines Boeing 747 which collided with a Kazakh Ilyushin IL-76 freighter near Delhi on Tuesday.

Achyut Shrestha, manager of the Air Express Private Limited, the general sales agent for the Saudi airline in Nepal, said he had confirmed 50 seats, including the group of 39, for Nepali passengers on the flight to Dhahran and Jeddah.
"We are unable at this moment to confirm how many (Nepali) passengers had actually boarded the aircraft," Shrestha said.
He said he had not received the passenger list from the airlines.
Many Nepali workers, mainly manual labourers, plumbers and drivers, travel to Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries in search of employment.
Government officials said there were about 8,500 Nepali workers in Saudi Arabia, but analysts said the number could be twice as high as many people went there without informing the government.

Nepal is one of the 10 poorest countries in the world and remittances from workers abroad are a major source of foreign exchange earnings in a country that receives 60 percent of its development budget in foreign aid.
Officials said they did not have records of the amount of money sent home by workers from the Middle East as they did not keep separate records of such transactions.
